summary: Aroostook County, ME tower: 1917-18 steel tower planned, 26-ft tower completed, 26-ft wood tower by 1920; FFLA lists standing, cab gone; status unclear.

facts.design: 26-foot wood tower listed in the 1920 inventory; a 48-foot steel tower was partly erected in 1917 with completion planned for 1918
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the structure as standing with the cab no longer in place. The lookout history lists the tower as removed, with no date. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says it is not known whether Squa Pan still stands.

access.note: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says its Squa Pan site is on private property; land status of the FFLA point was not confirmed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the structure as standing with its cab gone. The lookout history lists the tower as removed, with no date. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says it is not known whether Squa Pan still stands. The sources conflict, so the status is recorded as unknown and the conflict is flagged.

The FFLA point and the TopoZone point agree to rounding. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register describes a separate site, at a point south of those coordinates, on private property. We treat the two as different places, though the register suggests it may be the old Haystack Mountain tower.

The 1917 report describes a planned 48-foot steel tower. The 1918 report, as quoted, gives a 26-foot tower completed, and the 1920 inventory gives a 26-foot wood tower. We record 26 feet as the completed height.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on whether anything stands here now: FFLA says standing with cab gone, the lookout history says removed with no date, and the register says unknown. No staffing record was found. The 48-foot and 26-foot heights need the original 1917 and 1918 reports. Facebook posts by the FFLA Maine chapter mention a 1918 wooden tower and a Scopan Mountain name, but Facebook pages could not be read, so they are not cited. The FFLA list also has a separate Haystack Mountain log tower entry (gone); the register suggests a link, which we did not confirm. Worth a field check or an FFLA Maine chapter contact before publishing a status.
